'''Karen Ellen Smith''' (born 1965 in [[Red Bank, New Jersey]]){{r|born}} is an American mathematician, specializing in [[commutative algebra]] and [[algebraic geometry]]. She completed her bachelor's degree in mathematics at [[Princeton University]] before earning her PhD in mathematics at the [[University of Michigan]] in 1993. Currently she is the Keeler Professor of Mathematics at the University of Michigan. In addition to being a researcher in algebraic geometry and commutative algebra, Smith with others wrote the textbook ''[[An Invitation to Algebraic Geometry]]''.

==Biography==
Smith graduated in 1987 with a bachelor's degree in mathematics from [[Princeton University]], where she was influenced in her freshman year by [[Charles Fefferman]]. She was a high school mathematics teacher in the academic year 1987/1988. In 1988 she became a graduate student at the [[University of Michigan]],{{r|mactutor}} where in 1993 she earned her PhD with thesis ''Tight closure of parameter ideals and f-rationality'' under the supervision of [[Melvin Hochster]].{{r|mgp}} In the academic year 1993–1994 she was a postdoc at [[Purdue University]] working with [[Craig Huneke]]. In 1994 she became a [[C.L.E. Moore Instructor]] and then an associate professor at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]]. Since 1997 she has been a professor at the University of Michigan.{{r|mactutor}}

In 1991 she married the Finnish mathematician [[Juha Heinonen]].  He died in 2007.{{r|mactutor}}

==Honors==
In 2001 Smith won the [[Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize in Mathematics]] for her development of [[tight closure]] methods, introduced by Hochster and Huneke, in commutative algebra and her application of these methods in algebraic geometry. The prize committee specifically cited her papers "Tight closure of parameter ideals" (''[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]'' 1994), "F-rational rings have rational singularities" (''American J. Math.'' 1997, and, with Gennady Lyubeznik, "Weak and strong F-regularity are equivalent in graded rings" (''American J. Math.'', 1999).{{r|satter}}

In addition to the Satter Prize, Smith was the recipient of a 1997 Sloan Research Fellowship,<ref name=Sloan>{{citation|title=Sloan Past Fellows|url=http://www.sloan.org/sloan-research-fellowships/past-fellows/|website=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation|publisher=Sloan Foundation|accessdate=18 August 2015|archive-date=6 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161106043224/http://www.sloan.org/sloan-research-fellowships/past-fellows/|url-status=dead}}</ref> a Fulbright award, and a University of Michigan Faculty Recognition Award for outstanding contributions as a teacher, scholar and member of the University community.<ref name="Michigan award">{{citation|last1=University of Michigan|first1=Department of Mathematics|title=2005 News Archive|url=https://www.lsa.umich.edu/math/news/newsarchive/2005_ci|website=University of Michigan Department of Mathematics|publisher=University of Michigan|accessdate=17 August 2015|archive-date=31 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151031170917/http://www.lsa.umich.edu/math/news/newsarchive/2005_ci|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 1996, Smith was the first recipient of the [[AWM/MAA Falconer Lecture|Etta Z. Falconer Award]], where she presented the lecture "Calclulus mod p."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Falconer Lectures |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/falconer-lectures/ |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM) |language=en-US}}</ref>

Smith was selected to give the 2015 Earle Raymond Hedrick Lectures at the [[Mathematical Association of America]]'s MathFest.<ref name="Hedrick Lectures">{{citation|last1=|first1=|title=Invited Addresses: Earle Raymond Hedrick Lecture Series|url=http://www.maa.org/meetings/mathfest/program-details/2015/invited-addresses|website=Mathematical Association of America|accessdate=17 August 2015}}</ref>  Smith was chosen to give the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]]-[[American Mathematical Society]] 2016 [[Noether Lecture]] at the Joint Mathematics Meetings.<ref name="Noether Lecture">{{citation|title=Karen E. Smith Named 2016 Noether Lecturer|url=https://sites.google.com/site/awmmath/home/announcements/karenesmithnamed2016noetherlecturer|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160530172942/https://sites.google.com/site/awmmath/home/announcements/karenesmithnamed2016noetherlecturer|archive-date=2016-05-30|url-status=dead|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|accessdate=17 August 2015}}</ref>

In 2015 she was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to commutative algebra and algebraic geometry."<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=2015-11-16}}.</ref> She was named [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]] Clay Senior Scholar for 2012-2013.<ref>{{citation|last=MSRI|title=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|url=http://www.msri.org/|access-date=2021-06-07|website=www.msri.org}}</ref> In 2019, she was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2019-nas-election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190430143122/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2019-nas-election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 30, 2019|work=News from the National Academy of Sciences|title=National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and Foreign Associates; Historic Number of Women Elected to Its Membership|date=April 30, 2019}}</ref> The Association for Women in Mathematics has included her in the 2020 class of AWM Fellows for "her tireless support of women in mathematics; throughout her career, she has officially and unofficially mentored numerous female mathematicians at every level from undergraduate to full professor; she continues to be an incredibly strong role model for women everywhere".<ref>{{citation|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2020-awm-fellows/|title=2020 Class of AWM Fellows|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|accessdate=2019-11-08}}</ref> She was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2021.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2021|title=New Members Elected in 2021|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=2021-04-22}}</ref>

== Books ==
*''An Invitation to Algebraic Geometry'' (with Lauri Kahanpää, Pekka Kekäläinen, and William Traves, Universitext, Springer, 2000 and 2004).{{r|iag}}
*''Rational and Nearly Rational Varieties'' (with [[János Kollár]] and [[Alessio Corti]], Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics 92, Cambridge University Press, 2004).{{r|rnrv}}
